title: Verification efficiency and escalation
outOfScope: External CI provider configuration or credentials.
Release publication, package installation, and user-facing Japanese assessment reserved for WI-16/WI-17.
Changing the meaning of existing hard security or governance gates without explicit evidence and review.

sources.reason: WI-08 scope, acceptance, and required verification.
Current Task/PR/Release verification primitives and scope behavior.
Canonical check catalog and gate definitions.
Existing verification policy and context regression coverage.
Repository-required Work Item and lifecycle workflow.

riskAssessment.reason: Verification policy changes can accidentally weaken hard gates or cause stale cache reuse; fail closed on ambiguity and preserve existing hard checks.

executionDecision.reason: User authorized serial Work Item execution; implementation is bounded to verification orchestration and evidence policy.

preReviewWarnings: Review cache key completeness, invalidation, DAG ordering, escalation monotonicity, release Full Gate, and preservation of hard security gates.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Light, Standard, and Strict policies deterministically select focused or full verification, with Standard PR and Strict/Release always Full.
Cache keys include base, diff, command, tool, dependency, environment, and configuration digests; any changed input invalidates the cache.
Verification checks form an explicit DAG with deterministic ordering, deduplication, and fail-closed handling of unknown dependencies.
Deletion, CI/security/release changes, scope violations, unknown or injection signals, and test changes after failure automatically escalate and never downgrade.
Focused tests, full quality, governance checks, and verification documentation/check catalog/Make target alignment pass.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: Verification currently exposes useful primitives but does not yet provide one auditable policy for cost-efficient focused checks, content-addressed reuse, dependency ordering, and automatic escalation when risk increases.
constraints: Preserve existing hard gates and fail closed on ambiguity.
Keep verification deterministic and evidence-backed; cache reuse must never hide changed inputs.
Do not claim external Provider execution or release publication in this Work Item.
Keep Japanese/user-facing release evaluation out of scope until WI-16.
intent.rationale: A single explicit policy and evidence model should reduce redundant verification without allowing efficiency shortcuts to weaken security, release, or governance decisions.

declaredIntent.summary: Formalize deterministic Light/Standard/Strict verification selection, content-addressed cache invalidation, DAG ordering, and monotonic escalation without weakening hard gates.

rawUserRequest: Execute the approved AI Cockpit comprehensive remediation plan serially. For WI-08, formalize verification efficiency and escalation; complete each Work Item through Contract, implementation, verification, Summary/document alignment, PR, merge, closure, and branch cleanup.

rawRequestSource.reference: user-request: AI Cockpit comprehensive remediation instruction and continuation authorization

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The same complete input set reuses a cache entry, while any base/diff/command/tool/dependency/environment/config change invalidates it.
Deletion, CI/security/release changes, unknown or injection signals, scope violation, and test-after-failure cause escalation and never downgrade.
Strict and Release verification always execute the Full Gate with explicit DAG ordering and no unsafe cache shortcut.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User explicitly authorized serial execution of the complete remediation plan, including verification policy and documentation changes.
